name: extract_essence
description: Extract the dramatizable raw material from a scientific paper. Output is structured data, not narrative — creativity happens downstream.

summary.description: A clear, jargon-free summary of the research for a curious non-scientist. 2-4 sentences. Explain what the researchers did and what they found — plainly.

phenomenon.description: One sentence: what actually happens in nature or reality according to this paper. Not what the researchers did — what the universe does.

surprise.description: The counterintuitive element — the thing that defies obvious expectation. If the paper is entirely confirmatory and nothing surprises, write an empty string. Do not manufacture surprise.

stakes.description: Who or what is affected by this phenomenon, and why should anyone care. Be concrete — not 'it has implications for science' but what specifically hangs on this.

visual_elements.description:
3-8 things in the paper that are seeable, movable, or transformable — things a camera could follow. Write each item on its own line. Separate items with a newline character (\n), not commas or bullets. Each line is one complete description and may freely contain commas, parenthetical names, or abbreviations. Example:
Two honeycomb lattices stacked with a slight offset, one stretched relative to the other
Domain walls separating differently-stacked regions, sharpening as strain redistributes
Electrons confined to travel along a one-dimensional boundary channel

metaphor_surface.description:
3-5 everyday things this phenomenon rhymes with — not explanatory analogies, but things that share the same shape or feeling. Write each on its own line, separated by newlines. Each line names one thing only. Example:
A rope twisted until the strands snap into alignment
Frost forming along a crack between two cold surfaces
A tuning fork that only rings at one precise pitch

emotional_register.description: The primary feeling this underlying reality evokes, plus an optional secondary. Use single words or short phrases: awe, dread, wonder, grief, uncanny, quiet euphoria, existential vertigo, etc. Do not manufacture drama — if the paper's underlying reality is calm, say so.

inviolable_truths.description:
3-6 claims about this phenomenon that a film cannot contradict without ceasing to be about this phenomenon. Write each claim on its own line, separated by newlines. Each line is one complete sentence — one claim. Do not pack multiple claims into a single line. Example:
Topological channels only emerge after in-plane atomic relaxation sharpens the domain boundaries
An interlayer electric bias is required for the band gap to open and the topological protection to manifest
Two interface types — SP-stacked and AA-stacked — host modes with different spatial distributions

honest_difficulty.description:
Difficulty flags for what makes this paper hard to dramatize, one per line, separated by newlines. Format each line as 'flag_label: explanation'. One flag per line — do not pack multiple flags into one line. Leave empty string if the paper is filmable without significant obstacles. Common flags: no_visual_phenomenon, highly_technical, low_stakes_for_non_experts, no_narrative_arc, scale_problem, results_are_negative. Example:
highly_technical: the stakes require understanding band topology and valley Chern numbers to appreciate
scale_problem: the channels are nanoscale features invisible without specialized spectroscopy
